units.function: Mints and verifies short-lived HS256 Agent run tokens bound to company, control-plane instance, adapter, run and optional responsible user/scope.
units.dependencyDirection: Server auth adapter depends on process secrets/shared scope normalization; middleware consumes neutralized claims, but vendor adapter type remains in token claims.
units.keyDataModels: sub/company_id/adapter_type/run_id/responsible_user_id/key_scope/iat/exp/iss/aud/instance_id/jti claims and per-instance/per-company derived HMAC key.
units.lifecycle: Derive scoped signing key, mint token, verify signature/current-or-legacy key, parse claims, check expiry and conditional issuer/audience/instance, then create Agent actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 JWT tests and seven middleware tests cover signing, expiry, tenant/instance isolation, legacy fallback, run/header mismatch and responsible-user behavior. Gaps: custom JWT implementation, no maximum TTL/future-iat check, no replay/jti store, optional iss/aud/instance acceptance for legacy tokens, shared-secret rotation and a legacy raw-secret forgery window.
units.designRationale: Issue runtime-local credentials without storing raw provider sessions and harden fork/company isolation after a documented incident.
units.companyOsProblem: Connectors need short-lived secret-free runtime proof bound to exact work, capability, tenant and accountable human.
units.companyOsFit: Tenant/instance key separation and run/responsible-user binding are valuable. Company OS should use a standard signed-token library or asymmetric workload identity, mandatory issuer/audience/instance/action digest, bounded clock skew/TTL, key IDs/rotation and replay policy through Identity/Execution ports.
units.responsibilityConflict: A responsible_user_id claim is only identity context, not proof that the human approved the exact action, permissions, data grant or result.

units.function: Express composition root mounting every HTTP route, authentication/host/CSRF middleware, plugin host, UI, schedulers and background exporters.
units.dependencyDirection: A 752-line outer composition root imports virtually every route and plugin service plus static/Vite UI; inward modules do not import it.
units.keyDataModels: App options, deployment exposure, plugin lifecycle handles, host-service disposers and startup promises.
units.lifecycle: Configure parsing/logging/host/auth guards, mount routes, construct plugin/event/tool services, serve UI, start jobs/watchers/exporters and register cleanup.
units.testAssessment: Many route and app integration tests cover individual behavior, hostname gating and authorization. There is no concise composition-contract test proving route-by-route auth/size/origin policy; correctness is distributed across mount order and each router.
units.designRationale: Centralize startup wiring and keep route/service implementations independently testable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a narrow API service entry with consistent identity, authorization, size, idempotency and audit policies.
units.companyOsFit: Explicit composition is useful, but this root owns too many domains and background lifecycles. Company OS should compose bounded modules through uniform policy middleware and generated route metadata rather than rely on a long hand-ordered mount list.
units.responsibilityConflict: A route mounted outside the expected guard order can bypass organizational responsibility policy. Responsibility checks must be application invariants, not only Express topology.

units.function: Better Auth integration for email/password sessions, instance-scoped cookies, trusted origins and rate limiting.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer identity adapter depends on better-auth/Drizzle and Paperclip auth tables/config; middleware resolves its session shape.
units.keyDataModels: User/session/account/verification rows, session result, cookie prefix, base URL/trusted origins and rate-limit options.
units.lifecycle: Create auth instance against DB schema, issue session cookies, resolve sessions from request headers and map to board actor.
units.testAssessment: 17 focused Better Auth tests plus auth route/session tests cover cookie isolation, secure-cookie choices, trusted origins and rate-limit defaults. Email verification is disabled, sign-up defaults enabled, and enterprise OIDC/SAML/LDAP lifecycle is not represented.
units.designRationale: Provide a simple embedded identity system for local/self-hosted and authenticated modes.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed cloud and local enterprise need replaceable IdentityPort adapters with isolated token audience, tenant binding and independent audit.
units.companyOsFit: Cookie-instance isolation and origin derivation are useful references. Better Auth may be one adapter, never core; production profiles need explicit enrollment, verified identities and enterprise federation/provisioning/deprovisioning contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Authentication proves a principal session, not company role, accountable-human assignment or action approval; those remain Company OS domain checks.

units.function: Reads and validates the persisted JSON configuration with a shared Zod schema while warning about likely misspelled keys.
units.dependencyDirection: Server file adapter depends on shared config schema and local home-path resolution; domain code does not call it directly.
units.keyDataModels: Versionless PaperclipConfig JSON plus unknown-key suggestion warnings.
units.lifecycle: Resolve path, read/parse JSON, schema-validate, emit suggestions, return typed config or fail startup.
units.testAssessment: Focused config-file tests cover invalid JSON/schema and unknown-key preservation. They do not establish versioned migrations, atomic writes, rollback, provenance or concurrent writer behavior.
units.designRationale: Fail early on malformed operator configuration without deleting forward-compatible unknown keys.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles need validated, evolvable, supportable configuration with FDE overlays.
units.companyOsFit: Schema validation and preservation of unknown keys are useful. Company OS additionally needs explicit config schema versions, source precedence/provenance, secret-free support export and transactional migration/rollback.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configuration can change execution and security policy; consequential changes need an actor, digest and audit receipt rather than an anonymous file mutation.

units.function: Combines env, JSON config, defaults, path resolution and bind-mode detection into the runtime server configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Outer startup adapter depends on shared deployment enums and host filesystem/process commands; config values then fan into every service.
units.keyDataModels: Deployment mode/exposure/bind, auth origin, database/backup, secrets, storage, feedback export, scheduler, deletion and telemetry settings.
units.lifecycle: Load dotenv and file config, apply env precedence/defaults, optionally detect Tailscale, validate bind constraints and return one config object.
units.testAssessment: Configuration behavior is exercised indirectly and through bind/environment tests. Important env parsing is not uniformly strict: unknown enum values silently fall back, most booleans treat any non-'true' value as false, and numeric values use coercion/defaults. This can conceal operator mistakes.
units.designRationale: Offer zero-config local startup and flexible env overrides for containers and managed deployments.
units.companyOsProblem: Dual deployment profiles need the same business code but different adapters and enforceable security posture.
units.companyOsFit: The unified profile object and bind validation are useful. Company OS must parse every security-relevant env value strictly, reject invalid/unknown inputs, expose effective redacted config with provenance, and separate managed policy from mutable local preferences.
units.responsibilityConflict: Silent fallback can weaken intended identity, secret or exposure policy without a visible accountable decision.

units.function: Recognizes Postgres unique violations across Drizzle/driver cause chains and optional constraint names.
units.dependencyDirection: Server service helper depends only on error shapes/SQLSTATE and is called by transactional workflows.
units.keyDataModels: SQLSTATE 23505, constraint/constraint_name and bounded cause chain.
units.lifecycle: Walk up to four causes, detect unique violation and optional exact constraint, return boolean.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests cover wrapped driver variants, names/messages and unrelated failures. The bounded walk is deterministic and does not leak SQL text.
units.designRationale: Translate driver-specific wrapped conflicts into domain-level deduplication behavior.
units.companyOsProblem: Idempotent Connector/work/approval operations need portable conflict recognition at storage adapters.
units.companyOsFit: The cause-chain technique is useful inside a Postgres adapter, but Company OS application code should receive a neutral storage conflict code.
units.responsibilityConflict: None if kept in the storage adapter; a uniqueness conflict must not be interpreted as proof that the same human-approved action succeeded without digest comparison.

units.function: Minimal HTTP exception type and status-specific constructors.
units.dependencyDirection: Routes/services throw the server-specific HttpError; error middleware serializes it.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP status, English message and optional untyped details.
units.lifecycle: Construct error in service/route, propagate through Express, serialize message/details.
units.testAssessment: Behavior is covered through route/error-handler tests, but the type does not require a stable code, structured parameters, audience, retryability or safe/public distinction.
units.designRationale: Keep route errors concise and compatible with Express.
units.companyOsProblem: Independent Web, Connector SDK and future bilingual UI require stable machine contracts rather than English text matching.
units.companyOsFit: The status helpers are too weak. Company OS needs mandatory stable code, safe structured parameters, correlation ID, retry class and internal/public cause separation.
units.responsibilityConflict: Free-form details can accidentally expose sensitive evidence or misstate why a responsibility decision was denied.

units.function: Defines default JSON and company-portability upload ceilings, including an environment-overridable compressed ZIP limit.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport constants are imported by app/import routes; no inward domain dependency.
units.keyDataModels: 10 MiB default JSON, 64 MiB portable JSON and a 1 GiB default/64 GiB maximum compressed ZIP byte limit.
units.lifecycle: Parse the environment override at module load, clamp/fallback, configure whole-body parsers and derive decompression guards in import handling.
units.testAssessment: Six focused tests verify constants, override fallback and arithmetic clamping. The code explicitly states the entire upload is buffered in memory and allows up to 64 GiB, but tests do not exercise concurrency, process memory, slow uploads, authenticated tenant quotas or streaming decompression.
units.designRationale: Accept large real-world company packages in one request while bounding decompression arithmetic.
units.companyOsProblem: Enterprise import/export and FDE templates need large portable packages without turning the API into a memory/zip-bomb denial-of-service path.
units.companyOsFit: Separate route-specific limits are sensible, but the in-memory 1–64 GiB design is unacceptable. Company OS should stream to quarantined object storage, enforce compressed/uncompressed/file-count/ratio/tenant quotas, verify digest/signature, scan before activation and resume idempotently.
units.responsibilityConflict: Import mutates organization/data/permission state and needs an accountable initiator, validated manifest digest, preview and explicit apply receipt.

units.function: Full process startup and shutdown: instrumentation, Postgres, migrations, backups, auth, backfills, managed config, adapters, schedulers, WebSockets and listening.
units.dependencyDirection: A 1,536-line process entry imports DB migrations and most server services; it is the terminal composition layer.
units.keyDataModels: StartedServer, migration state, embedded/external DB runtime, deployment/auth state, managed config, backup health and shutdown coordination.
units.lifecycle: Initialize telemetry/secrets, provision DB, inspect/reconcile/apply migrations, validate deployment contracts, backfill/reconcile state, build app and realtime, start schedulers/backups, load adapters, listen, then coordinated shutdown.
units.testAssessment: Startup, shutdown, migration, managed-config, worktree and feedback-export behaviors have focused tests, but the entire production sequence is not exercised as one failure-matrix. Non-interactive startup automatically approves pending migrations unless PAPERCLIP_MIGRATION_PROMPT=never, increasing unattended upgrade risk.
units.designRationale: Make a single command self-healing and easy to operate, including embedded Postgres and compatibility backfills.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted enterprise needs reliable migration, backup, recovery, health, upgrade and rollback semantics.
units.companyOsFit: Refusal to run on stale schema, migration inspection, startup ordering and coordinated cleanup are important references. Company OS should split the orchestrator into testable phases, require an explicit production migration policy, support preflight/backup/rollback receipts and avoid behavior-changing data backfills hidden in process startup.
units.responsibilityConflict: Automatic schema/backfill changes are consequential administrative actions and require operator policy, immutable evidence and rollback ownership.

units.function: Masks current OS usernames and home-directory paths recursively before log export.
units.dependencyDirection: Logging adapter depends on process/env/path data; business records remain untouched.
units.keyDataModels: Candidate usernames/home dirs, replacement token and recursively redacted values.
units.lifecycle: Discover candidate identity strings, replace longest paths then bounded username tokens, recurse plain objects/arrays.
units.testAssessment: Four focused tests cover path, token-boundary, nested and disabled behavior. It cannot discover every PII path or guarantee redaction of non-plain objects/buffers.
units.designRationale: Prevent workstation identity leakage in diagnostic logs while preserving useful paths.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE support bundles and managed-cloud telemetry must not exfiltrate local employee/device identity.
units.companyOsFit: Useful defense-in-depth for support export. Company OS should combine structured sensitivity labels, allowlisted fields and tenant policy; original user input/evidence stays in its governed store rather than being mutated.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redaction must preserve evidence integrity by storing original and redacted derivative separately with a digest/provenance link.

units.function: HTTP actor resolution, cloud trusted headers, CSRF/origin guard, hostname/DNS-rebinding guard, trust-proxy parsing, validation, logging/redaction, compression and error serialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Transport layer depends on DB/shared/services and writes a rich Express actor used by routes; some authorization semantics therefore live in middleware rather than application services.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor sources, memberships/on-behalf-of snapshot, key scope/run ID, cloud stack identity, trusted host/origin/proxy config and structured HTTP error response.
units.lifecycle: Resolve implicit/session/cloud/API-key/JWT actor, validate host and browser mutation origin, execute route, sanitize logs and serialize errors.
units.testAssessment: Dedicated tests cover Agent auth, 17 cloud-tenant cases, board mutation, private host, trust proxy, errors and redaction. Important issues remain: local_trusted is implicit instance admin; Cloud uses one static trusted-header token; private-host and board-origin code reads X-Forwarded-Host directly rather than only through the configured trusted-proxy interpretation; stable error codes are optional.
units.designRationale: Normalize many transport identities once and provide backwards-compatible on-behalf-of human context to all routes.
units.companyOsProblem: Every request needs tenant/principal/capability context, but responsibility/data authorization must remain uniform across HTTP, events and Connector dispatch.
units.companyOsFit: Fail-closed missing responsible user, active membership snapshots and stale elevation cleanup are strong patterns. Company OS should issue a neutral PrincipalContext from IdentityPort, use short-lived audience-bound service identity, derive forwarded host only from trusted proxy state, and enforce responsibility inside application use cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: onBehalfOfUserId is valuable but still only a delegation context. It must not substitute for an exact responsibility contract and high-risk approval digest.

units.function: Server package manifest, build/test entry points and dependency ownership for the Paperclip control-plane process.
units.dependencyDirection: The server directly imports DB/shared/plugin SDK plus every built-in Agent adapter and many infrastructure vendors, making it both composition root and runtime owner.
units.keyDataModels: No domain data; package scripts, published exports and dependency graph.
units.lifecycle: Build/typecheck/test the server and bundle UI/adapter/plugin artifacts into the distributable package.
units.testAssessment: Vitest configuration and a large server suite exist, but the manifest itself has no dependency-policy or architecture test preventing domain-to-vendor coupling. Several runtime packages use compatible ranges rather than exact pins.
units.designRationale: One deployable server simplifies self-hosted installation and makes built-in adapters available without separate services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a simple deployable profile while preserving replaceable model, Agent, storage, identity and execution ports.
units.companyOsFit: The single-service packaging is operationally useful for an early self-hosted profile, but Company OS must keep vendor adapters out of inward layers and preferably out of the core server package dependency graph.
units.responsibilityConflict: Directly owning execution vendors in the control-plane package encourages transport credentials and sessions to leak across responsibility boundaries.

units.function: Company event WebSocket subscriptions and one-time authenticated SSH terminal bridging for custom sandbox-image setup.
units.dependencyDirection: Realtime transport bypasses Express middleware and implements separate DB/session/key authorization; terminal path depends on custom-image services, ephemeral session store and ssh2.
units.keyDataModels: Company upgrade context, session/API key identity, event subscription, terminal setup/session token, pinned SSH host hash, resize/input/output frames and connection registry.
units.lifecycle: Intercept HTTP upgrade, independently authorize, bind company subscription or validate a short-lived terminal session, bridge frames/SSH, enforce expiry/heartbeat and clean up sockets/sessions.
units.testAssessment: Three live-event tests and eight terminal tests cover cross-company denial, sessions, query/header token behavior, one-time auth, expiry, host verification and cleanup. Live events accept long-lived Agent API keys in URL query parameters, do not accept scoped run JWTs, and do not repeat Agent status/responsible-human checks from HTTP middleware; query credentials may leak through intermediaries despite application log care.
units.designRationale: Support browser-compatible realtime and interactive setup while keeping terminal connection payloads ephemeral.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss needs realtime projections, while local execution setup may require interactive operator intervention without leaking credentials.
units.companyOsFit: One-time terminal tokens, host-key pinning, expiry and cleanup are good patterns. Company OS should use one shared authorization service for HTTP/WebSocket/events, prohibit long-lived credentials in URLs, use short-lived audience/work-scoped tickets and publish only sanitized projection events with resume cursors.
units.responsibilityConflict: Realtime delivery and terminal transport must not create authority. An interactive human identity and any resulting runtime/config mutation need an exact audited responsibility record.

units.function: Recursively removes credential-shaped fields, command flags, JSON fragments and JWT-shaped values from events/log text.
units.dependencyDirection: Server safety helper imports command redaction from adapter-utils and is used across audit/log/run surfaces.
units.keyDataModels: Secret field-name regex, secret/user-secret/plain bindings, CLI argv rules, JWT pattern and REDACTED marker.
units.lifecycle: Inspect field/type/value, preserve safe secret references, redact secret material and command args, recursively sanitize plain data.
units.testAssessment: Eight core tests plus HTTP/run/comment redaction suites cover nested payloads, flags, bindings, JWTs and audit exceptions. Regex/field-name detection remains inherently incomplete and can both miss novel credentials and over-redact ordinary data.
units.designRationale: Apply one broad defense across heterogeneous Agent/provider payloads without requiring every caller to remember secret fields.
units.companyOsProblem: Control-plane events must exclude credentials/private sessions/reasoning while retaining evidence and original business output in authorized stores.
units.companyOsFit: Reference preservation and structured traversal are strong. Company OS should make sensitivity typed at ingestion and deny unknown payload shapes; heuristic redaction remains a final guard, not the primary security boundary.
units.responsibilityConflict: Redacted audit text cannot replace source evidence. Responsibility records must point to immutable authorized evidence digests and record the redaction transform.

units.function: Shared route authorization helpers for actor type, instance/company access, cross-tenant existence-oracle protection, actor audit fields and secret-consumer context.
units.dependencyDirection: Express route layer consumes the middleware actor and server authorization shadow-mode setting; services do not depend on these helpers, so some security invariants exist only at HTTP call sites.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor, company membership and viewer role, on-behalf-of responsible user snapshot, actor source/run/key IDs and secret consumer context.
units.lifecycle: Authenticate actor, hide inaccessible resource existence, intersect Agent company scope with an optional responsible-user membership, enforce read/write role, derive audit/secret context, then call a service.
units.testAssessment: The authorization suites cover 19 company-access cases, five secret-context cases and a static route scan preventing known existence-oracle regressions. Gaps: HTTP method is used as the write-risk proxy; static source scanning cannot prove every dynamic path; stable denial codes are inconsistent; shadow mode intentionally permits responsible-user denials; and an Agent whose onBehalfOfUserId is absent skips the human-membership intersection entirely.
units.designRationale: Centralize backwards-compatible company scoping and prevent 403/404 differences from leaking cross-tenant resource existence.
units.companyOsProblem: Every use case must combine tenant, principal, role, responsible human, data grant, work contract and risk-specific approval without leaking object existence.
units.companyOsFit: The indistinguishable not-found pattern, server-derived secret consumer and human/Agent permission intersection are strong references. Company OS must enforce them inside application use cases across every transport, require an accountable human for formal Agent work, remove shadow bypass from production and authorize named actions rather than HTTP verbs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Paperclip treats responsible human context as optional for some JWT/legacy paths and permits a shadow mode. Company OS requires every formal Agent action to resolve an active responsibility contract and exact human owner before execution.

units.function: Secret-provider SPI with local AES-256-GCM storage, AWS Secrets Manager managed/reference support, health checks, discovery and GCP/Vault metadata-only stubs.
units.dependencyDirection: Server provider adapters implement a shared SecretProviderModule and depend on filesystem/crypto/AWS credentials; service/routes own DB metadata and bindings separately.
units.keyDataModels: Provider descriptor/capabilities, prepared version material/fingerprint, runtime/write context, external/provider version refs, stable provider client errors and health/backup guidance.
units.lifecycle: Validate provider, create/link/version/resolve/rotate/archive material, retain DB metadata/fingerprints and report health; local key comes from env/file, AWS uses default credential chain and recovery-window deletion.
units.testAssessment: Registry/local tests and 18 AWS tests cover capabilities, key permissions, request signing, credential cache, managed/external versions, listing/discovery, error mapping and deletion. GCP/Vault are non-resolving stubs; local key creation/permission is best effort and lacks envelope encryption/rotation; provider tests are largely mocked.
units.designRationale: Separate secret metadata/bindings from storage material and support both easy local operation and cloud vault custody.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent/model/data connectors require scoped credential custody, rotation, audit and local-enterprise vault integration without exposing values to the control plane.
units.companyOsFit: Provider SPI, version fingerprints, external refs, stable client codes and health/backup guidance are strong. Company OS needs owner/purpose/consumer/action-bound access leases, real Vault/China-cloud adapters, envelope/KMS rotation, no value return to browser/control plane, and fail-closed profile policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Resolving a secret proves technical access, not that its use was authorized for this work/data purpose. Every resolution must be policy-checked and audited against the accountable human and runtime proof.

units.function: StorageService/StorageProvider abstraction with company-prefixed object keys and local-disk or S3 implementations.
units.dependencyDirection: Routes/services consume a server-local storage interface; provider registry selects filesystem or AWS SDK from runtime config.
units.keyDataModels: Provider ID, object key, content type/length, byte range, ETag/mtime and PutFile SHA-256 metadata.
units.lifecycle: Validate file metadata, generate tenant/date/UUID key, hash and put bytes, read/head/range/delete after company-prefix check, switch provider by deployment config.
units.testAssessment: Four local-provider tests cover round-trip, range, cross-company prefix and idempotent delete. No S3 provider tests were found. Local containment is lexical only: directory/file symlinks under the storage root are followed by write/read/head/delete, with no realpath or O_NOFOLLOW defense. Range validity, atomic temp cleanup after failure, content digest on read and concurrent overwrite semantics are not tested.
units.designRationale: Keep asset storage replaceable and tenant-scoped while making local self-hosting zero-config.
units.companyOsProblem: Evidence/artifacts and imports need independent cloud/local storage with tenant isolation, integrity, retention and lifecycle policy.
units.companyOsFit: The provider/service split and returned content digest are useful. Company OS should own an Evidence/Artifact Store port with immutable version IDs, digest verification, encryption/retention/legal-hold metadata and streaming; local storage must use descriptor-based no-follow containment and S3 must have integration/consistency tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: A tenant-prefixed key is not evidence provenance. Every artifact must bind to work, executor, data authorization, collection method and immutable digest before appearing in the responsibility chain.

units.function: Limits Docker build context by excluding Git, local state, dependencies, logs and caches.
units.dependencyDirection: Constrains the root Docker build input.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; excludes local `.paperclip` and database state.
units.lifecycle: Applied before Docker stages and therefore part of secret/data leakage prevention.
units.testAssessment: A Docker dependency-stage check exists, but build-context negative assertions are not comprehensive.
units.designRationale: Reduce image context, cache invalidation and accidental local-data inclusion.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must keep credentials, production data and local execution state out of images.
units.companyOsFit: Directly relevant as a pattern, with Company OS-specific paths and secret checks.
units.responsibilityConflict: Leaked local state could expose evidence, credentials or responsibility records.

units.function: Documents local database, server/UI and authentication/signing environment variables.
units.dependencyDirection: Feeds server configuration conventions; contains development placeholder secrets.
units.keyDataModels: Connection URL and secret-bearing configuration keys.
units.lifecycle: Copied by operators for development; unsafe values must never become production defaults.
units.testAssessment: Configuration parsing is tested elsewhere, but the example itself can drift and has no schema-generation link.
units.designRationale: Minimize local startup friction.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs profile-specific, validated configuration without real credentials.
units.companyOsFit: The discoverability fits; Company OS should generate examples from typed config and reject placeholder secrets in production.
units.responsibilityConflict: A signing secret affects action authority and must be deployment-owned, rotated and audience-bound.

units.function: Excludes dependencies, builds, environment files, runtime state, reports, tool scratch and worktrees.
units.dependencyDirection: Repository hygiene only; several negations keep audit scripts tracked.
units.keyDataModels: Names local state classes that must not enter source control.
units.lifecycle: Protects normal development, but cannot replace secret scanning or data-classification gates.
units.testAssessment: Git status and secret scanners detect some mistakes; ignored files are inherently less visible to repository checks.
units.designRationale: Separate source from generated, runtime and developer-specific state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs explicit source/runtime/data separation.
units.companyOsFit: Use the principle, not the exact paths.
units.responsibilityConflict: Formal evidence must not be treated as disposable ignored scratch; production evidence belongs in governed storage.

units.function: Normalizes multiple contributor identities for Git statistics.
units.dependencyDirection: Affects contributor reporting, not product runtime.
units.keyDataModels: Contributor identity aliases.
units.lifecycle: Maintained as author addresses change.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated test; Git tooling consumes it directly.
units.designRationale: Avoid double-counting contributors in release and maintenance metrics.
units.companyOsProblem: Open-source governance also needs accurate contributor provenance.
units.companyOsFit: Useful repository practice but not reusable product code.
units.responsibilityConflict: Git authorship is not organizational approval or accountable-human identity.

units.function: Enables automatic peer installation.
units.dependencyDirection: Changes dependency resolution for the whole workspace.
units.keyDataModels: No business data.
units.lifecycle: Applied at install time and can change the resolved graph when peer ranges change.
units.testAssessment: Frozen lockfile checks constrain normal CI, but standalone excluded plugins are separate.
units.designRationale: Reduce manual peer dependency friction in a plugin-heavy monorepo.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deterministic extension dependency resolution.
units.companyOsFit: Convenient but implicit; prefer explicit peer ownership and frozen lock validation.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; implicit dependency installation is a supply-chain concern.

units.function: Grants MIT rights to Paperclip source subject to copyright and permission-notice preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: Applies to first-party Paperclip code unless a nested dependency or asset states separate terms.
units.keyDataModels: No runtime data; copyright and license text are provenance records.
units.lifecycle: Any substantial copied portion must retain the notice in Company OS distribution and provenance.
units.testAssessment: License presence is mechanically checked by Company OS research governance; per-asset and dependency licenses still require their own review.
units.designRationale: Permit broad reuse without warranty while preserving attribution.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs legal selective reuse and auditable notices.
units.companyOsFit: Compatible with selective legal reuse, but does not grant Paperclip trademarks, logos or third-party asset rights.
units.responsibilityConflict: None.

units.function: Root command graph, toolchain pin, dependency overrides and patched-dependency ownership.
units.dependencyDirection: Orchestrates all workspaces through pnpm; does not contain a runtime domain boundary.
units.keyDataModels: No business records; release package map, workspace scripts and dependency resolution are operational metadata.
units.lifecycle: Install links the Plugin SDK; build/typecheck/test fan out; database, release, smoke, visual and eval commands have separate lanes.
units.testAssessment: Many scripts have focused tests and CI callers, but the root has no single proof that every declared command is exercised.
units.designRationale: Centralize a large monorepo while preserving package-local builds and split slow or environment-sensitive test lanes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs reproducible workspace orchestration, split quality gates and explicit release commands.
units.companyOsFit: The lane separation fits; the very large command surface and upstream-local patches would be excessive at current Company OS scale.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; scripts must not become an alternate path around production responsibility gates.

units.function: Carries local changes to `acpx` process/session behavior and `embedded-postgres` locale/environment propagation.
units.dependencyDirection: Root package resolution injects these patches into third-party distributions; product runtime behavior therefore depends on local fork deltas.
units.keyDataModels: ACPX session options/process callbacks and embedded Postgres process environment, not Company OS domain records.
units.lifecycle: Every dependency upgrade must rebase and retest patches; `acpx` has a packaging test while embedded Postgres behavior has package-level tests.
units.testAssessment: There is explicit ACPX patch packaging coverage, but patches still enlarge the long-term maintenance and supply-chain review surface.
units.designRationale: Fill missing upstream hooks for process supervision, environment transfer, Windows parsing and portable embedded Postgres startup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will face child-process supervision, platform quoting and local database portability problems.
units.companyOsFit: The problems matter, but copying compiled distribution patches would be brittle; use supported upstream APIs or owned adapters.
units.responsibilityConflict: Agent spawn hooks and environment transfer are security-critical and must bind to an authorized work/run lease.

units.function: Pins the root workspace dependency graph and records patched dependency resolution.
units.dependencyDirection: Covers included pnpm workspaces, not deliberately excluded standalone sandbox providers.
units.keyDataModels: Package versions, integrity hashes, peer snapshots and importer dependency edges.
units.lifecycle: Updated by dependency changes and a dedicated refresh workflow; consumed by frozen installs and release images.
units.testAssessment: PR scripts validate lock changes and production audit was run; vulnerability results are time- and advisory-database-specific.
units.designRationale: Reproducible monorepo installs with explicit dependency overrides.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs reproducible builds, SBOM input and vulnerability gates.
units.companyOsFit: Required pattern, but no Paperclip version or importer should be copied.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; compromised dependencies can bypass all application responsibility semantics.

units.function: Defines workspace membership and deliberately excludes sandbox providers and one orchestration smoke fixture from the root lock graph.
units.dependencyDirection: Packages join the root graph by glob; excluded packages install independently and can drift from the canonical lock.
units.keyDataModels: No business data; workspace membership is build provenance.
units.lifecycle: Root install covers core packages while standalone plugins own separate installation and lock behavior.
units.testAssessment: Release and plugin smoke tests cover some exclusions; there is no universal cross-lock compatibility proof.

units.function: Runs Codex by CLI or ACP with model profiles, output/process inactivity monitoring, isolated homes, device login and identity-keyed credential cache/copyback.

units.function: Invokes durable Cursor Cloud Agents through the vendor SDK and maps Paperclip heartbeats to remote runs.

units.function: Runs Cursor Agent CLI locally or remotely with session resume, stream parsing, skills and trust controls.

units.function: Runs Gemini CLI through ACP or CLI with fallback, session parsing, remote execution and skill materialization.

units.testAssessment: Six focused tests cover ACP, fallback, remote behavior, parsing and UI config; vendor auth and quota contracts are mostly probe-driven.

units.companyOsProblem: Connector negotiation must express optional engine versions and deterministic fallback without changing work identity.

units.function: Runs Grok CLI as a single-turn/session-resumable coding Agent and normalizes turn boundaries and transcripts.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector conformance tests for progress/result ordering and duplicate terminal events.

units.function: Provides local and gateway Hermes adapters plus an Agent-facing task-bridge skill that can call Paperclip REST APIs.

units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs to separate execution connectors from inbound delegated-control connectors and give each distinct scopes/audiences.

units.function: Compatibility/re-export shim exposing the gateway implementation from the Hermes package.

units.keyDataModels: None beyond re-exported Hermes gateway types.

units.function: Connects to OpenClaw over WebSocket, performs gateway/device authentication, optional auto-pairing, session routing and wake/result normalization.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and `ws`; adapter config may contain shared tokens/passwords and defaults to broad `operator.admin` scopes.
units.keyDataModels: Gateway connection challenge, device identity, shared auth, scopes, session key strategy, wait request and normalized runtime service reports.
units.lifecycle: Resolve credentials/device → open/challenge/connect → optionally approve pairing → send Agent request → wait/stream → normalize result → close or retain session route.
units.testAssessment: Two large tests cover execution protocol and UI config, but broad scopes, first-connect auto-approval and reconnect/cancel races warrant dedicated security/property tests.
units.designRationale: Integrate a remote Agent runtime whose native protocol has its own pairing and session semantics.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector bootstrap/pairing, capability attenuation, revocation, reconnect and remote identity proof.
units.companyOsFit: The problem is important; the Paperclip/OpenClaw wire implementation must remain adapter-specific and credentials must be secret references.
units.responsibilityConflict: Default `operator.admin` and automatic pairing are incompatible with least privilege unless a human approves the exact connector enrollment and capability set.

units.function: Runs OpenCode CLI with multi-provider model discovery, session resume, runtime config/skills and optional remote sandbox execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; installer executes an unpinned remote script and server expands credential placeholders into provider config.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model ID, session/cwd, generated opencode config, skill set and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Install/probe → discover model → generate runtime config with resolved refs → execute/resume → parse result → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests cover execution, remote path, models, parsing and runtime config; installer integrity and generated-secret cleanup are not equivalent to a full threat-model test.
units.designRationale: Support a provider-agnostic Agent CLI and avoid installing several unused architecture binaries.
units.companyOsProblem: Execution nodes need signed/pinned tool acquisition and ephemeral secret materialization with destruction proof.
units.companyOsFit: Multi-provider selection belongs above the adapter, but unverified `curl | bash`, permission bypass default and secret-bearing generated files conflict with enterprise defaults.

units.function: Runs Pi coding Agent with provider/model discovery, sessions, skills and generated provider runtime configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; provider secret placeholders are resolved server-side into configuration shipped to local or remote execution.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model, thinking level, session/cwd, models.json/provider config, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Probe pinned npm CLI → discover/validate model → materialize provider config/skills → execute/resume → parse → restore.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover remote execution, models, parser and runtime config; cleanup, cancellation and secret residue need stronger tests.
units.designRationale: Expose Pi's multi-provider tool runtime through the same adapter surface.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs provider-neutral model routing while keeping credentials inside the execution plane.
units.companyOsFit: Pinned installer is better than remote script, but direct provider config materialization stays an adapter implementation detail.
units.responsibilityConflict: All tools are enabled by default; Company OS capability leases and data egress policy must constrain the actual tool set per work action.

units.function: Postgres persistence package with 110+ table definitions, 210 tracked SQL migration files at the pin, external/embedded runtime selection, migration inspection/reconciliation, seed, backup and restore.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared DTO vocabulary, Drizzle, postgres.js and patched embedded Postgres. Server and CLI import concrete tables and `Db`, so schema types penetrate service code.
units.keyDataModels: Companies, memberships, Agents, issues/goals/runs, workspaces, approvals, budgets/costs, documents/decisions, Secrets, tools, plugins, environments, routines, pipelines and audit/activity tables. Tool access alone defines over twenty related tables.
units.lifecycle: Resolve database target → bootstrap external or embedded Postgres → inspect/reconcile migration journal → apply ordered SQL → serve transactional tables → backup via pg_dump or JS stream → retain/restore with sanitization.
units.testAssessment: 24 tests cover client options, embedded startup, backup, migration safety and selected high-risk schema migrations. The migration corpus and many schemas have only targeted or integration-level coverage; restore compatibility across every historical release is not exhaustively proven.
units.designRationale: Support a low-friction local install and a serious Postgres deployment while accumulating product features through explicit migrations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent schemas, migration safety, tenant isolation, backup/restore, offline/self-hosted bootstrap, audit retention and extension storage.
units.companyOsFit: Operational patterns are valuable, but the schema is Paperclip's product and cannot be copied. Company OS should use bounded schemas/modules and an outbox rather than direct table imports across all services.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generic approval payload and Agent-to-Agent hierarchy cannot enforce Company OS responsibility. Activity logging is separate from immutable responsibility/evidence state, and local-trusted bootstrap must not weaken production identity.

units.function: MCP server for reading and mutating Google Sheets through service-account credentials over stdio or HTTP.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends directly on Google APIs, MCP SDK and Zod; credential JSON/path and HTTP auth are resolved at the process boundary.
units.keyDataModels: Service-account configuration, spreadsheet/range requests, tool responses, HTTP auth config and secret-redaction values.
units.lifecycle: Load/validate credentials → construct Google client → register Sheets tools → receive stdio/HTTP call → execute external API → redact and return result.
units.testAssessment: Five tests cover config, Google client, tools and HTTP server. They are fixture/mocked tests and do not prove enterprise domain allowlists, row-level data contracts, DLP or Google audit reconciliation.
units.designRationale: Provide a concrete external data/tool integration with both local and hosted transports.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs company data connectors, authorization contracts, egress firewall checks, credential leasing and evidence of external reads/writes.
units.companyOsFit: Useful threat-model input, but a standalone MCP credential/config model is insufficient for Company OS data governance.
units.responsibilityConflict: Spreadsheet writes can be business actions. They require data-scope authorization, output classification, exact action approval when risky and immutable evidence, not merely possession of a service account.

units.function: Deterministic in-memory key/value MCP fixture with stdio startup and basic tools.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends only on MCP SDK and Zod; no Paperclip server or production store.
units.keyDataModels: In-memory key/value entries and MCP tool request/response.
units.lifecycle: Start process → register get/set/list/delete-like fixture tools → mutate process memory → discard state on exit.
units.testAssessment: Three tests cover store/tool/server behavior; it is intentionally not persistence, tenancy or security evidence.
units.designRationale: Provide a small deterministic MCP target for integration and smoke tests.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Demo and Connector conformance tests need credential-free deterministic external-system fixtures.
units.companyOsFit: The pattern fits, but it must be labeled fixture/Demo and isolated from formal data or Agent claims.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fixture writes must never be projected as real enterprise actions or evidence.

units.function: Stdio MCP façade over Paperclip REST APIs, exposing Agent/company/task/goal/approval/document/workspace runtime read and mutation tools.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on MCP SDK, shared schemas and Zod; reads API URL/token/company/Agent/run identity from environment and delegates authorization to the server.
units.keyDataModels: MCP tool definition, API client config, company/Agent defaults, issue/goal/approval IDs and formatted text/error responses.
units.lifecycle: Read environment credential/context → register dozens of tools → validate input → call REST endpoint → format result/error over stdio.
units.testAssessment: Only one tools test covers a broad mutable surface; API/schema drift, permission denial, cross-tenant identifiers, idempotency and destructive tool semantics need much stronger contract coverage.
units.designRationale: Give coding Agents a standard tool protocol without embedding REST details into every Agent prompt/runtime.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a Data/Tool Connector boundary and safe Agent-facing control tools.
units.companyOsFit: MCP can be one adapter, never the core Connector contract. Company OS tools must be generated from owned API contracts and expose stable machine errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: The same token surface can create/patch/checkout work, request approvals and control runtime services. Company OS must attenuate each call to an exact capability lease, risk policy and accountable-human contract.

units.function: Minimal authoring fixture proving a manifest, capability declarations, event subscription, scoped plugin state, a health/data/action bridge and one dashboard slot.
units.dependencyDirection: Example worker and UI depend on the Paperclip Plugin SDK and host bridge; the host does not depend on example internals.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest v1, issue.created event, issue-scoped state key and health/action response. It owns no durable business model.
units.lifecycle: Install/build → host validates manifest and starts worker → setup registers event/data/action handlers → issue event writes state → host probes health → uninstall removes the fixture.
units.testAssessment: Two focused tests cover manifest capabilities and event/state behavior. They are appropriate smoke coverage but do not test install, upgrade, isolation, failure recovery or UI behavior.
units.designRationale: Give plugin authors the smallest executable contract test instead of requiring them to understand the full host.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a tiny Connector/plugin authoring smoke fixture and compatibility test that third parties can run without production credentials.
units.companyOsFit: The executable contract-test pattern fits, but Company OS must use its own Connector/extension API and deterministic fixture vocabulary.
units.responsibilityConflict: The sample only observes issue creation and cannot authorize execution, so it does not model accountable humans or responsibility contracts; it must never be presented as a real Agent.

units.function: Example project file browser/editor and comment-file-link UI backed by direct host filesystem reads and writes.
units.dependencyDirection: Worker depends on Plugin SDK project/comment APIs but directly imports node:fs/path, bypassing a mediated filesystem capability; UI depends on Paperclip slot and bridge contracts.
units.keyDataModels: Project workspace path, directory entry, file content and comment-derived path token. Files remain owned by the host filesystem rather than a plugin data store.
units.lifecycle: Read workspace path from host → resolve lexical child path → list/read/write local files → render project tabs/comment actions. It defines no revision, locking, atomic write, rollback or deletion lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: No tests across 1,114 source lines. Traversal is checked lexically, but read/write follow symlinks because paths are not realpath-verified or opened no-follow; an in-workspace symlink can expose or overwrite an external file.
units.designRationale: Demonstrate several UI extension slots with an immediately understandable local-workspace feature.
units.companyOsProblem: An Agent Boss may need evidence/artifact browsing, but production access must be capability-mediated, authorized, size-limited, auditable and safe against symlinks and races.
units.companyOsFit: The UI-slot illustration is understandable; the filesystem implementation is unacceptable for Company OS security and self-hosted enterprise boundaries.
units.responsibilityConflict: A plugin can mutate files without a declared filesystem-write capability, approval binding, actor/evidence record or responsibility contract, allowing unaccountable external effects.

units.function: Small UI-only dashboard-widget example with a worker health probe.

units.keyDataModels: Manifest v1, dashboardWidget slot and health result; no business or persistent data.
units.lifecycle: Install/build → register widget → start health-only worker → render static widget → uninstall.
units.testAssessment: No tests, though the entire package is only 85 TypeScript/build-source lines. It demonstrates shape, not compatibility assurance.
units.designRationale: Minimize the first successful plugin authoring experience.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS extension authors need a minimal independently buildable UI extension example.
units.companyOsFit: The small-example principle fits, while Paperclip slots, branding and runtime types do not.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; the static widget must remain a fixture and cannot imply execution or responsibility.

units.function: Broad development-only demonstrator for host read/write APIs, Agents/sessions, events, jobs, webhooks, HTTP, Secrets, tools, workspace access, local processes, telemetry and many UI slots.

units.lifecycle: Install → register broad handlers/surfaces → receive events/jobs/webhooks/actions → optionally resolve secret refs, call outbound HTTP and spawn curated host processes → keep some volatile diagnostics until worker restart.

units.companyOsProblem: A compatibility lab needs coverage of the entire extension API, including negative permission cases and host-version drift.
units.companyOsFit: Useful only as a development conformance fixture. Company OS must split fixtures by capability, test denial, and execute untrusted extensions outside the host process.
units.responsibilityConflict: A single plugin can pause/resume/invoke Agents, create work, read Secrets, call HTTP and spawn local processes without a Company OS human approval and responsibility envelope. That aggregation violates least privilege for production.

units.function: Orchestration-grade smoke fixture for plugin database migrations, scoped API routes, issue creation/relations/documents/subtree summaries and idempotent wakeup.

units.testAssessment: Three focused tests cover manifest/database/route shape, orchestration path and route dispatch. It does not cover migration rollback, concurrent duplicate requests, uninstall retention, authorization denial or failure compensation after partial writes.
