units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs compatibility fixtures proving extension migrations, actor propagation, idempotency and orchestration projections across upgrades.
units.companyOsFit: The smoke-test strategy fits. Company OS must add a human principal, responsibility contract, exact approval/action digest and compensation assertions before issuing executable work.
units.responsibilityConflict: The board-or-agent route can create and wake Agent work with an optional Agent/user actor but no mandatory accountable human or responsibility contract.

units.function: Paperclip environment-driver plugin that delegates Cloudflare Sandbox lifecycle and command execution to a separately deployed authenticated bridge.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK contracts and a custom HTTP/SSE bridge protocol; Cloudflare SDK/runtime is isolated in the bridge template.
units.keyDataModels: Secret-ref bridge token, endpoint/API prefix, keep-alive/sleep/reuse/session options, opaque provider lease ID, sentinel metadata and normalized execute result.
units.lifecycle: Validate configuration and bridge health, acquire/resume lease through bridge, prepare workspace/sentinel, execute with bounded HTTP timeout and optional SSE, then release or destroy.
units.testAssessment: 31 tests across six files cover configuration, bridge HTTP errors/timeouts, lifecycle, streaming, command forwarding and metadata. They mock the bridge and do not prove Cloudflare network isolation, bridge deployment security, retry/idempotency under ambiguous HTTP failure, or real provider cleanup.
units.designRationale: Keep vendor SDK and edge-runtime requirements outside the host process while exposing one environment-driver contract.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs provider-neutral local/remote execution nodes without placing vendor credentials or private sessions in its control plane.
units.companyOsFit: The narrow bridge and secret-ref pattern are useful. Company OS should own a versioned execution-node protocol with idempotency keys, authenticated workload identity, structured stable error codes, health/attestation and reconciliation rather than inherit Paperclip's endpoint and lease vocabulary.
units.responsibilityConflict: The bridge authenticates a bearer token but does not bind commands to an approved action, data grant, accountable human or runtime proof. That binding belongs above the provider adapter.

units.function: Deployable Cloudflare Worker/Durable Object bridge implementing health, probe, lease acquire/resume/release/destroy and command execution endpoints.
units.dependencyDirection: Bridge depends directly on @cloudflare/sandbox; Paperclip reaches it only through HTTP/SSE. No Company OS-neutral protocol package exists.
units.keyDataModels: Bearer-authenticated JSON requests, provider lease/sandbox IDs, named/default sessions, sentinel file, timeout/result envelope and SSE stdout/stderr/complete events.
units.lifecycle: Constant-time bearer verification, resolve/create sandbox and session, ensure workspace, write/verify sentinel, stage stdin, run quoted login-shell command, clean timed-out sessions and temporary files, then keep alive or destroy.
units.testAssessment: 16 tests cover auth, ID helpers, session-scoped sentinel operations, quoting/env validation, stdin cleanup, SSE and timeout-shaped behavior. There are no authorization-scope tests, replay/idempotency tests, rate limits, schema validation/fuzzing, audit correlation, provider integration, or reconciliation after partial failure.
units.designRationale: Bridge edge-only provider APIs behind a small service boundary and avoid loading Cloudflare-specific code into the main server.
units.companyOsProblem: A customer-local execution node or vendor bridge needs a small, replaceable protocol and reliable lease lifecycle.
units.companyOsFit: Separation and constant-time secret comparison are useful. Company OS needs signed short-lived workload tokens, request/version/schema validation, idempotency, cancellation, capability/attestation and action/evidence correlation; generic 500 responses must not leak raw internal messages.
units.responsibilityConflict: A static bridge token authorizes all operations and carries no principal/action scope. It cannot itself prove a human-approved responsibility chain.

units.function: Daytona-backed environment driver with image/snapshot creation, native file sync, command streaming/polling, reusable stop/start leases, sentinels and cleanup recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and exact @daytonaio/sdk 0.203.0; Daytona credentials are resolved through secret-ref/environment configuration.
units.keyDataModels: API endpoint/key, image-or-snapshot choice, workspace/timeouts/auto-delete/reuse, opaque sandbox ID, lease metadata, file manifest and command result.
units.lifecycle: Validate mutually exclusive image/snapshot, create or start sandbox, verify/write sentinel, sync files, execute and stream/poll, stop reusable leases or delete ephemeral ones, and delete on fatal preparation failures.
units.testAssessment: 131 focused tests in one large test file cover validation, lifecycle, sentinel recovery, command/streaming behavior, path canonicalization, symlinks, binary/file sync, cleanup and SDK edge cases. The suite is mock-heavy; no real-provider integration or concurrency/reconciliation proof exists. Documentation still promises an advisory bubblewrap wrapper that current source explicitly removed.
units.designRationale: Map a rich provider SDK behind the shared environment-driver lifecycle while exploiting native stop/start and file APIs.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs robust provider adapters, workspace transfer and cleanup without allowing provider types or credentials into core/application.
units.companyOsFit: Lifecycle failure handling, sentinel ownership, file canonicalization and exact SDK pinning are strong references. The implementation is vendor/Paperclip coupled and its documentation drift shows that isolation claims require executable compatibility evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A valid lease executes arbitrary commands without an action/approval/data-grant binding. Company OS must classify and authorize before dispatch and record exact runtime/image/permission attestation afterward.

units.function: Thin E2B environment driver for template-based sandbox creation, command execution, timeout extension, reuse and kill.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and e2b ^2.19.0; E2B API key is a secret-ref or environment fallback.
units.keyDataModels: API key, template, workdir, timeout/reuse settings, sandbox ID, shell metadata and normalized execution output.
units.lifecycle: Create or reconnect by sandbox ID, set timeout, ensure workspace, execute shell command with stdin/env/cwd, retain reusable lease or kill it.
units.testAssessment: 19 tests cover validation, acquire/resume/release/destroy, timeout, command construction and errors. Coverage is appropriate for a thin adapter but lacks real provider, network/isolation, concurrent reuse, ambiguous failure and cleanup reconciliation tests.
units.designRationale: Expose E2B as another installable implementation of one environment-driver contract with minimal local policy.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may offer optional vendor execution connectors while preserving runtime neutrality.
units.companyOsFit: Provider lifecycle mapping is a useful reference, but the code offers little differentiated infrastructure and remains coupled to Paperclip contracts and a floating compatible SDK range.
units.responsibilityConflict: No human responsibility or exact permission/evidence binding exists at this layer; it must remain a subordinate execution adapter.

units.function: exe.dev remote-VM environment driver using the provider HTTPS API for VM lifecycle and SSH for setup, file transfer and command execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK plus host ssh/scp/ssh-agent/key files and exe.dev HTTPS endpoints; it has no provider SDK dependency.
units.keyDataModels: API key/base URL, region/image, SSH user/key/agent, setup command, workdir/timeouts/reuse, VM name/address and lease metadata.
units.lifecycle: Create VM via API, wait for SSH, optionally install runtime with a default remote setup command, create sentinel, execute/sync through SSH, retain a reusable live VM or delete it; probe can create and delete a billed VM.
units.testAssessment: 35 mocked tests cover config, API lifecycle, SSH argv/quoting, key/agent auth, setup, streaming and cleanup. They do not prove host-key trust, provider behavior, network policy, VM isolation, cost containment, concurrent reuse or recovery from an unknown create/delete outcome.
units.designRationale: Use ubiquitous HTTPS and SSH instead of a proprietary SDK, allowing the provider to remain a standalone installable plugin.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted/local enterprise deployments may need SSH-based execution nodes, but they must be governed and safely enrolled.
units.companyOsFit: Argument-array discipline and transport separation are worth studying. Direct host key paths/ssh-agent fallback, remote bootstrap scripts, always-live reuse and a paid probe are unsafe defaults for Company OS. A local node should use explicit enrollment, pinned host identity, prepared images and cost/network policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Possession of host SSH credentials effectively grants broad machine authority without responsibility-contract scope. Company OS must not treat transport access as organizational authorization.

units.function: Kubernetes execution provider with per-company namespaces, quotas, restricted pod policy, deny-all networking, scoped egress, image allowlists, per-run secrets, alpha agent-sandbox CR and batch Job backends.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK, @kubernetes/client-node ^1.0.0 and zod. A SandboxOrchestrator interface separates alpha agents.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1 and stable batch/v1 backends.
units.keyDataModels: Validated cluster/provider config, tenant namespace/resources, image policy, egress grant, workload/secret owner references, opaque lease metadata, backend capability, command/file-sync result and cleanup state.
units.lifecycle: Validate config/image/network grants, ensure tenant namespace/service account/quota/restricted policies, create workload and scoped egress, create owner-bound secret, wait for pod, exec/sync when supported, then release or forcibly reconcile every resource.
units.testAssessment: 195 tests across 21 files cover manifest/config, image allowlist, namespace/RBAC/quota, NetworkPolicy/Cilium, pod/CR/job manifests, secret ownership, lease cleanup, upload interception, readiness, execution and multiple failure paths. It is the strongest provider suite reviewed, but provider integration is manual smoke testing; the default CRD is alpha and Job mode cannot support multi-command adapter installation.
units.designRationale: Use Kubernetes-native tenant and workload boundaries, with a swap interface for evolving sandbox backends and defensive cleanup independent of owner-reference success.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted enterprise needs enforceable tenant isolation, image/data-egress policy, secret lifetime, resource quotas and recoverable local execution.
units.companyOsFit: Tenant orchestration, image allowlist, owner-bound secrets, deny-all baseline, per-work scoped egress and force cleanup are strong patterns. Company OS must define its own execution/data-authorization contracts, fail closed when exact FQDN enforcement is required, pin/attest images, and not make an alpha CRD canonical. Source correctly disables service-account token automount despite stale README text.
units.responsibilityConflict: Infrastructure isolation does not decide whether a human authorized the action or data egress. Every workload must carry an opaque responsibility/action digest and produce secret-free runtime proof; broad standard-NetworkPolicy public egress cannot satisfy an exact data contract.

units.function: Modal environment driver for registry-image sandboxes, optional network blocking, command/file execution and detach-based lease reuse.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and Modal client APIs; token ID/secret are stored as secret-ref configuration.
units.keyDataModels: Token pair, environment/image/workdir/timeouts, blockNetwork/reuse flags, Modal sandbox ID, tags, shell metadata and normalized command result.
units.lifecycle: Authenticate, resolve registry image, create or reconnect sandbox, ensure workspace, execute and stage stdin, detach a reusable lease or terminate it.
units.testAssessment: 26 mocked tests cover authentication, validation, create/resume/detach/terminate, command quoting, stdin and timeout behavior. They do not prove provider network blocking, image provenance, concurrent detach/reconnect, maximum lifetime or cleanup reconciliation.
units.designRationale: Exploit Modal's image and sandbox primitives while translating detach semantics into the shared lease contract.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit capability negotiation because providers differ on pause, detach, network and persistence semantics.
units.companyOsFit: The honest distinction between detach and pause plus optional network blocking is a useful lifecycle reference. The adapter is otherwise vendor/Paperclip specific and should not be copied wholesale.
units.responsibilityConflict: Network blocking is configuration rather than a responsibility/data authorization proof, and detach extends the lifetime of credentials/workspace. Company OS must record retention and accountable approval separately.

units.function: Thin Novita Agent Sandbox driver with template creation, command execution, auto-pause, pause/resume reuse and kill.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin depends on Paperclip Plugin SDK and novita-sandbox ^1.0.3-b2; API key is resolved through secret-ref or environment fallback.
units.keyDataModels: API key, template, workdir, request/sandbox timeouts, beta auto-pause/reuse flags, sandbox ID and shell/result metadata.
units.lifecycle: Create from template or reconnect, set timeout, detect shell, ensure workspace, execute, pause reusable lease or kill it.
units.testAssessment: Eight mocked tests cover the main lifecycle and execution path. There is insufficient coverage for beta SDK drift, command quoting/adversarial inputs, ambiguous failures, concurrency, cleanup, network/isolation or real provider behavior.
units.designRationale: Offer the provider through the same environment-driver surface with minimal policy and optional reuse.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector capability declarations must distinguish provider-specific preview/beta lifecycle behavior.
units.companyOsFit: Pause/resume capability vocabulary is useful, but the adapter is thin, beta-dependent and under-tested. It should be an optional future connector after its SDK and semantics mature.
units.responsibilityConflict: Pausing preserves state and potentially sensitive data without a retention contract or accountable approval; provider lifecycle alone cannot supply that governance.

units.function: Cross-provider sandbox image/runtime requirements and capability matrix for Paperclip's first-party providers.
units.dependencyDirection: Documentation describes assumptions imposed on external images, provider APIs and the Paperclip environment driver contract; no code depends on it mechanically.
units.keyDataModels: Provider capability matrix, image prerequisites, command/file-sync constraints, lease reuse semantics and advisory isolation notes.
units.lifecycle: Operator supplies image/provider configuration, plugin probes prerequisites, lease executes, and release either pauses/stops/detaches or destroys according to provider semantics.
units.testAssessment: No executable conformance test binds this document to providers. It currently says Daytona degrades to plain execution when bubblewrap is absent, while Daytona source and DIRECTORY-CONSTRAINT-FINDINGS say the wrapper was removed entirely. It also says Kubernetes workloads automount a service-account token, while both current pod builders set automountServiceAccountToken=false.
units.designRationale: Centralize provider-specific prerequisites so images are prebuilt and runtime execution avoids expensive setup.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a machine-verifiable execution-profile contract covering isolation, image provenance, network policy, secrets, lifecycle, capabilities and runtime attestation.
units.companyOsFit: The matrix format and immutable-image principle are useful, but prose that drifts from code cannot be the trust source. Required confinement must fail closed and be demonstrated by compatibility tests and short-lived secret-free attestations.
units.responsibilityConflict: Calling isolation advisory while continuing execution obscures who accepted the risk. Company OS must surface the effective trust tier and bind any exception to an accountable human and exact policy digest.

units.function: CLI scaffolder for a Paperclip plugin package and its worker/manifest/UI entrypoints.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on the Plugin SDK and emits packages coupled to its v1 manifest/build layout.
units.keyDataModels: Template package metadata and entrypoint paths, not business data.
units.lifecycle: Prompt/arguments → create files → install/build against SDK → plugin is later installed by the host.
units.testAssessment: One entrypoint test checks generated structure; it does not validate production distribution, signing or sandboxing.
units.designRationale: Reduce authoring errors and make the preferred extension shape easy to start.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will need a Connector/extension starter with conformance and provenance defaults.
units.companyOsFit: The scaffolding idea fits, but emitted Paperclip manifest/types and branding do not.
units.responsibilityConflict: Generated templates should default to no capabilities and require explicit human-reviewed grants.

units.function: Deterministic local fake sandbox provider that exercises environment-driver leases, setup sessions, templates and command execution without external infrastructure.
units.dependencyDirection: Implements Plugin SDK environment-driver contracts and writes only to temporary local directories.
units.keyDataModels: Fake lease ID, environment/session ID, template reference, redacted connection metadata and deterministic driver config.
units.lifecycle: Validate/probe → allocate temp lease → execute/sync → release or retain → capture template/setup → clean up.
units.testAssessment: One focused test covers the integrated provider lifecycle. It is intentionally not a security sandbox and should not be used as production proof.
units.designRationale: Make provider-plugin integration deterministic and credential-free in CI.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a deterministic Connector/execution-node conformance fixture that is never represented as a real Agent or sandbox.
units.companyOsFit: Strong testing pattern; Company OS should build its own neutral fixture against its Connector SDK.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fixture actions must remain Demo/test-only and must not mint formal identity, credentials or responsibility records.

units.function: Large first-party knowledge plugin that captures sources, maintains file-backed multi-space wikis, distills Paperclip work into cited pages, runs Agent-backed queries/maintenance and exposes API/tools/UI.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin owns namespaced relational metadata and local wiki files but consumes broad Paperclip issue/comment/document/event/Agent/session/routine/skill APIs and UI slots; it is not a neutral knowledge service.
units.keyDataModels: Wiki/space/source/page bindings, operation and distillation cursors/snapshots, source windows, generated patch proposals, managed Agent/routine/skill bindings and file hash/provenance records across three SQL migrations.
units.lifecycle: Bootstrap files/schema → capture manual or Paperclip sources → debounce/cursor source windows → redact secret-like material → create visible operation work → generate cited review patches → verify hashes/policy → approve or conditionally auto-apply → advance cursor only on success → lint/archive/repair spaces.
units.testAssessment: 101 tests across 20,193 source lines cover schema/surfaces, UI, event isolation, cursor success rules, provenance, secret suppression, bounded backfill, review patches, authenticated-public auto-apply refusal, stale hashes, size limits, protected files and Agent sessions. Remaining risk is the very large single plugin/worker, Paperclip-specific integration breadth and limited real database/filesystem/concurrency E2E evidence.
units.designRationale: Keep optional knowledge behavior outside core while making source provenance, generated changes and maintenance visible as ordinary work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs governed institutional knowledge, original-source evidence, FDE template learning and safe improvement proposals without storing private reasoning as control-plane truth.
units.companyOsFit: Cursor-after-success, source-window provenance, redaction, stale-hash checks and review-before-write are strong patterns. Company OS should separate knowledge authorization, evidence, generated proposals and execution, and avoid Paperclip issue/Agent/UI coupling.
units.responsibilityConflict: Default auto-apply can be allowed in trusted local modes, while Company OS must bind any consequential knowledge/policy mutation to a classified action, exact digest and accountable human approval. LLM synthesis is evidence-derived content, not authoritative responsibility proof.

units.function: Read-only workspace change projection that computes bounded Git staged/unstaged/untracked or base-ref diffs and renders them in workspace tabs.
units.dependencyDirection: Core diff service depends on Node filesystem/child_process and small Paperclip workspace metadata types; worker/UI adapt it to Plugin SDK and @pierre/diffs.
units.keyDataModels: Validated diff query, file status/patch/warning, byte/file caps, workspace metadata and summarized statistics. It does not persist a separate database.
units.lifecycle: Resolve and realpath workspace/repo → normalize filters/base ref → invoke git with argument arrays/timeouts/buffers → realpath/no-follow untracked files → cap patches and aggregate warnings → validate bridge response → render; no mutation occurs.
units.testAssessment: 26 tests across 2,999 source lines cover contracts, UI model/error state, staged/unstaged/rename/delete/untracked/binary/oversized data, caps, filters, base refs and external-symlink non-disclosure. TOCTOU remains possible between realpath and open on hostile filesystems, and real Git/plugin integration is local-only rather than sandbox-attested.
units.designRationale: Keep expensive and security-sensitive filesystem/Git computation in a plugin-local service with strict output bounds rather than the browser.
units.companyOsProblem: Evidence review needs safe bounded workspace/artifact change projections without importing an Agent vendor session or exposing arbitrary host files.
units.companyOsFit: The service shape, execFile argument discipline, realpath/no-follow checks, structured warnings and caps are strong. Company OS should place it behind an evidence/artifact reader port and execution-node attestation rather than a trusted Web plugin.
units.responsibilityConflict: Read-only projection does not approve or publish changes. Company OS must bind the resulting digest and source workspace/run to the responsibility record before a human approves publication.

units.function: Official worker/UI/testing/build SDK with versioned JSON-RPC, manifest and lifecycle types, capability-gated host clients, events, jobs, tools, state/entities, local folders, Secrets, Agent sessions and same-origin React slots.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared and Zod with React as peer. Plugins compile against it; the server implements the host side and the UI loads SDK-compatible bundles.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest v1, JSON-RPC request/result/error, invocation metadata, domain event, job, tool, state scope, entity, UI slot/host context, environment driver and Agent session.
units.lifecycle: Validate manifest/version → install package → start worker process → setup registrations → capability-check worker↔host RPC → deliver events/jobs/API/tool calls → health/config changes → bounded shutdown. UI bundles load separately in the browser.
units.testAssessment: Six SDK tests cover host client, worker host, protocol/UI/testing paths, plus extensive server tests. The README explicitly calls deployment early: workers and UI are trusted, dynamic install assumes single-node writable filesystem/npm/network, and multi-instance artifact distribution is unresolved.
units.designRationale: Provide one discoverable extension API while keeping persistence, auth and core mutations behind host services.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs version negotiation, capability declarations, extension isolation, durable event delivery, package provenance, multi-node distribution and separate Connector versus UI-extension trust models.
units.companyOsFit: Fail-closed operations, manifest validation and host-mediated resources fit. The API is Paperclip-domain-wide, same-origin UI is not isolated, and resolved secrets can cross into a trusted worker; Company OS needs a narrower capability/lease protocol.
units.responsibilityConflict: Plugins can create/update work, invoke Agents and respond to approvals through broad capabilities. Company OS must require accountable-human sponsorship and exact action authorization, not merely a manifest capability.

units.function: Cross-runtime public vocabulary for server, UI, CLI, adapters and plugins: constants, DTO types, Zod input validators, API paths, portability, feature/app definitions and presentation helpers.
units.dependencyDirection: Nearly every workspace depends inward on this package; it depends mainly on Zod. A 2,300+ line barrel and 1,400+ line constants file make it both contract layer and product-wide coupling hub.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, issue, goal, run, approval, budget, secret, tool, plugin, environment, decision, document, artifact, project, membership and live-event DTOs plus their enums/validators.
units.lifecycle: Request input is parsed into shared DTOs, persisted through separate DB schema, returned to UI/plugins and sometimes serialized for company portability. Generated app and telemetry files are regenerated from source catalogs.
units.testAssessment: 51 tests cover 15 validator groups and many focused helpers. Many pure type files and the enormous enum/barrel surface have indirect compile-time coverage only; server and UI can therefore become lockstep coupled.
units.designRationale: Prevent duplicated request/response shapes across a TypeScript monorepo and make provider adapters share product terminology.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs stable wire contracts, validators, portable IDs and machine error codes across Web, API, Connector and deployments.
units.companyOsFit: The schema-first approach fits, but Company OS must separate domain value objects, public API DTOs, Connector wire types and UI copy instead of one universal shared package.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several enums expose `require_approval`, risk and principal concepts without enforcing exact action/contract/human/evidence bindings; shared labels and English denial messages must not become authority contracts.

units.function: Builds and validates a catalog of bundled/optional Agent skills, files, assets, sources, trust levels and compatibility metadata.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on shared frontmatter/schema helpers; generated manifest is consumed by server/UI and release packaging.
units.keyDataModels: CatalogSkill, source reference, file kind, trust level (`markdown_only`, `assets`, `scripts_executables`), compatibility and generated manifest.
units.lifecycle: Scan catalog files → parse frontmatter → validate slugs/source/file graph → hash/package metadata → compare or write deterministic generated manifest → ship catalog.
units.testAssessment: Five tests cover builder, frontmatter, packaged artifacts, release-content contracts and shipped manifest. Runtime skill execution safety remains outside the catalog package.
units.designRationale: Make instructional and executable Agent assets discoverable and release-verifiable with explicit trust classification.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS FDE templates and later training need versioned, provenance-aware capabilities with trust and compatibility metadata.
units.companyOsFit: Trust-tier and deterministic manifest ideas are valuable; Paperclip skills/content/brand should not be copied wholesale.
units.responsibilityConflict: A skill is guidance or executable material, not authority. Installation and use must be bounded by Agent role, data scope, human owner and signed version.

units.function: Builds and validates deployable team templates containing Agents, projects, tasks, local/external skills and environment inputs.
units.dependencyDirection: Reads the skills catalog generated manifest and team markdown/frontmatter; generated team manifest is consumed by product onboarding/import paths.
units.keyDataModels: CatalogTeam schema `agentcompanies/v1`, Agent/project/task graph, reportsTo/owner/assignee references, skill requirements, source refs and secret/plain environment inputs.
units.lifecycle: Scan team bundle → parse entity files → validate graph and referenced skills → summarize env inputs/trust → write deterministic catalog manifest → import into a company.
units.testAssessment: Two tests cover builder and shipped catalog. Human roles, responsibility contracts, approval policies, data contracts, template upgrades and rollback are not represented or tested.
units.designRationale: Turn a repeatable Agent organization and workflow into a distributable onboarding artifact.
units.companyOsProblem: This directly anticipates Company OS FDE industry templates, implementation repeatability and template provenance.
units.companyOsFit: The catalog pipeline is a strong reference, but Company OS templates must include humans, departments, accountable roles, responsibility contracts, data authorization, risk/approval policies and migration versions.
units.responsibilityConflict: Current reporting/ownership references are Agent-centric. Importing them as formal organization state would omit accountable humans and may silently grant tools/secrets.
